cls: Weak antiseptic (eye wash, ear drops, vaginal capsules)
pharm: Weak antiseptic (eye wash, ear drops, vaginal capsules)
summary: Boric acid is a weak antiseptic and astringent. Its main evidence-based use is 600 mg vaginal capsules for recurrent or azole-resistant (non-albicans) vulvovaginal candidiasis. It is toxic if swallowed or absorbed through large areas of broken skin, especially in infants.
indications: Recurrent or azole-resistant vulvovaginal candidiasis (vaginal capsules)
Eye washes and ear drops (low concentration)
admin: Use only as the finished product directs

absolute: Infants and young children (do not apply to nappy area or large areas)

lact: Safety not established; weigh benefit against unknown risk

serious: Systemic boron toxicity if ingested or absorbed: vomiting, diarrhoea, erythroderma, seizures, renal failure

counsel: Keep away from children: fatal if swallowed
missed: Take it when remembered unless the next dose is due; do not double up.
overdose: Supportive; haemodialysis in severe boron poisoning.
refs: Martindale: The Complete Drug Reference (Pharmaceutical Press)
